reviews.title: Great game, ruined by ads
reviews.text: So sick and tired of good games being ruined by an utterly insane amount of ads. DO NOT FORCE ADS. I understand these games are free and need to make money. But there are ways to use ads in a way that is consumer friendly and show that your company cares about the player, rather than rinsing them of their time showing zero respect. Use ads as gameplay elements but they should ALWAYS be a choice. Rewards should give you lots as a thanks for supporting the game. This method might not seem good short term, but long term you will retain loyal players rather than quick 1 or 2 time players that play then delete. I’d even consider spending money to support the developers if it wasn’t so anti consumer.

reviews.title: Good game for the most part
reviews.text: This game is simple enough - just tap where you want to shoot. However, I have a few issues with it. Firstly, the chances of spinning and getting a gun or character are abysmal. Multiple times, the needle has landed near the grand prize, only to barely miss it and magnetize to the next prize, which never seems to happen with any other prize. Another problem is that the weapons become way too expensive as you progress through the game, despite still earning only $800-$900 per level. Additionally, I understand that this is a small-time developer, but I'm disappointed that none of the levels are different as you progress, aside from the color schemes.

reviews.title: Ninety Five Theses: mobile game edition
reviews.text:
I would recommend reading my review if you want an in-depth overview of Run N Gun. I could go on and on about this game, but it would be much easier to make a bullet point list. I have done my best to love this game, but it’s flaws are impossible to look past.

+ Amazing gameplay. Max Payne-style jumping and shooting is a lot of fun, with the enemy diversity (even guys disguised as hostages) and environment tricks. Weapon diversity with the stat simplicity is great- each weapon has an identity, especially the Assassin’s tracer-like rounds. I *might* play it more for the dopamine.
- The gameplay is soured by a lack of difficulty. Multiple times later on I tried to barely miss a shot (as I did unintentionally in the early game), and it autocorrected towards the enemy/moving gas can. You don’t have to lead your shots on moving targets. Bonus levels are only difficult from the border of the screen threatening to make some zombies unkillable which *almost* caught me off guard. Also, riot shields break in one hit which seems like it’s just a reskin of the 2 health guys except they can sometimes block hazards you want to shoot at.
- Levels get very repetitive. Tapping somehow keeps its satisfaction, but after Market (fourth world, each of which is like 4+ 1 minute levels long), every tile set repeats- just slightly better in art style and with the enemy diversity. Enemies and hazards are replaced, but it’s basically the same levels with firefights mixed up between each other (I got like the same fight twice in Airport 2). AFAIK there’s only one boss in the game- the first world’s.
- Rigged RNG. No, really. Every “Price is Right” cash box reward will give you the least possible amount of the 3. The bonus levels end with a roulette “chance” to get the shotty- it always slides right off. I know my chances well, and I don’t think 50% chance would go 10+ bonus levels without being gotten. There are other people with the same problem, by the way. I didn’t watch the ads for these rewards, but they probably are necessary to get the big rewards. Speaking of which!
- ADS. A problem with a majority of new mobile games. Finished a level? Watch this ad for more outfit cards! Didn’t want to? Watch this necessary ad between every level. Starting a new level? Watch this ad and try this mid/late-game gun for a level for FREE! Didn’t get the “RNG” reward you wanted? I could go on. By the way, the daily reward is negligible and just gets you to look at the shop.
/ Simplistic mobile game art style was probably just so they could produce this game more easily. 😕
/ The first skin you get, you are forced to without a CoC-like option to save your outfit cards… default even looks 10x better, that first skin looks like a test skin lol. Other ones look good at least 🤷‍♂️

Conclusion: Like an original flash game (glorious “murder stick figures” gameplay) but with App Store predatory practices (even crappy ads for the game!) injected. Intentionally easy and forgiving for people with slow reaction time/aim, so you zoom through and watch MORE ads. The ads are just too numerous unless you somehow avoid them (likely paying to turn them off)… For anyone who reads this, I would recommend Sierra 7 instead- a great flash game ported to mobile that’s basically this but better and in FPS style.

Closing statement time. This game reminds me of Darktide for some reason: The gameplay is glorious and almost addictive, but the dev team clearly has lazy shortcomings and the micro transaction team, well… BRUH. Skins are fan service (goodness I want that space marine unlock, too bad it’s probably level 100. I think the soldier is more than dripped out though) which isn’t bad until you consider the unlock methods. I love the gameplay and progression, but everything surrounding it is crumbling (Fatshark please add game pass steam cross play I beg).
